the most relevant proteins in learning ability were found to be: 1) NMDA receptor subunit 2B (GRIN2B) 2) NMDA Receptor 1 (GRIN1) 3) Glutamate Receptor, Metabotropic 5 (GRM5) 4) Glutamate receptor metabotropic 1 (GRM1) 5) Glutamate receptors 6) Glutamate Ionotropic Receptors 7)
the most relevant proteins for learning ability in DS mice were: 1) Cyp2b1, 2) Cyp2c11, 3) Cyp2e1, 4) Cyp2f2, 5) Cyp3a11, 6) Cyp2d22, 7) Gsta1, 8) Gsta2, 9) Gstp1.

1) the most important proteins that could be used as biomarkers for Down Syndrome are the ones related to the learning ability; 2) the most promising bioinformatic model to study protein profiles and their relation to the learning ability of Down Syndrome patients is the K Nearest Neighbour; 3) Neural Network is a good alternative to the K Nearest Neighbor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach in the field of bioinformatics, where a supervised machine learning model is used to predict the learning ability of a mouse model of Down syndrome.
the development of a predictive tool to be used in the follow up of DS patients after treatment with memamine.
the application of bioinformatics to the analysis of the protein profile in DS mouse model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the most accurate models are K NN and Neural network with the most relevant protein attributes being: A1BG, APOA1, C3, C4BPA, CFB, CFD, FGA, FGB and HBA2.
our results show that the most important attributes for the prediction of protein profiles are the protein name, the gene name, the chromosome and the location.
the K NN and NN models are promising tools for future studies in the field of learning and memory abilities in DS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our study provides an accurate tool to evaluate learning abilities and to determine the most suitable proteins to be used as biomarkers for DS.
the most relevant proteins were found to be: APOE, C3, CCL5, CCL2, IL-1B, IL-6, IL-1a, TNF-a and CCL4.

the most relevant proteins for the prediction of learning ability are: 1) Nucleolin, 2) 14-3-3 protein, 3) Calmodulin 4) Calreticulin 5) 14- 3-3 protein 6) 14- -3 protein 7) Annexin 8) Calnexin 9) Calreticuline.
The main takeaway from our work is that
protein attribute based models can be a promising predictive tool for Down syndrome and other diseases.

the application of machine learning algorithms to the study of protein profiles in a Down Syndrome mouse model can be useful to identify potential biomarkers and can be used to predict protein expression levels.
the application of machine learning techniques to protein data can provide a useful predictive tool in a DS mouse model.
